record_type_quote: We successfully replicate the prior Nie et al cross-validation results using a newer version of their data that is publicly available.

targets.authors: Nie Z, Vairavan S, Narayan VA, Ye J, Li QS.
targets.title: Predictive modeling of treatment resistant depression using data from STAR*D and an independent clinical study.
targets.evidence_quote: We sought to independently replicate the cross-validation findings by Nie et al [15] on the STAR*D dataset, and then externally validate their methodology on another new dataset from the Canadian Biomarker Integration Network in Depression (CAN-BIND)-1 study [26], a multicentre study to discover multi-modal (neuroimaging, electrophysiological, molecular, clinical) biomarkers to predict treatment response in patients with MDD.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: The highest balanced accuracy was higher in our study compared to Nie et al (73% versus 71%, respectively). Similarly, our highest AUC was higher at 0.81 versus 0.78, respectively. The z-score of Nie et al’s results in our distributions ranges from -0.4 to -34.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Regardless, our slightly improved performance is unlikely to be clinically significant, and we instead interpret our results as a successful replication supporting the findings of Nie et al. and our own implementation of data processing and machine learning methods.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Primary replication reanalyses STAR*D original participants using updated release and reconstructed pipeline; original numerical performance not exactly recovered, with large standardized differences, hence computational issues despite authors calling substantive replication successful. Alternative holdout, feature sets and preprocessing retain predictive performance; authors judge differences clinically unimportant. External CAN-BIND data provide an additional new-sample replication, not evidence on reproduction robustness. Single record_type cannot represent both components, so reproduction prioritizes the direct original-data check. Robustness judgment has uncertainty because some alternate response criteria have reduced performance.
